facts.claim: SAI1 and eDMA setup at 0x80001BE0 (called once, from 0x80000BEC). Transmit: TCD0-3 (eDMA TCD base 0x400E9000) each write a 32-bit word (ATTR 0x202, SOFF 4, DOFF 0) to TDR0-3 of SAI1 (0x40384020-0x4038402C), 64 bytes per request, 64 major iterations, channels linked 0->1->2->3, only channel 3 interrupts at the end of the major loop (CSR 0x0A); DMAMUX channel 0 = source 20 (SAI1 transmit). Receive: TCD4 reads RDR0 of SAI1 (SADDR 0x403840A0, SOFF 0) as 16-bit units (ATTR 0x101), 32 bytes per request, DOFF 2, 64 major iterations, CSR 0x0A; DMAMUX channel 4 = source 19 (SAI1 receive). SAI1 registers set in the same function: TCR1 16, TCR2 0x40000000 (SYNC=01, transmit synchronous with receive), TCR3 0xF0000 (four transmit lanes), TCR4 0x100F1F38 (frame 16 words, sync width 32, MSB first), TCR5 0x1F1F1300 (words 32 bits, first bit 19, so 20 significant bits per slot); RCSR 0x10000001, RCR1 16, RCR2 0, RCR3 0x10000 (one receive lane), RCR4 0x100F1F10 (16 words, MSB first), RCR5 0x1F1F0F00 (words 32 bits, first bit 15, so 16 significant bits per slot). So every frame the second processor sends 16 slots back on one lane, of which APP1 keeps 16 bits each; one receive bank is 64 frames x 32 bytes = 0x800 bytes, one transmit bank per lane 64 x 64 bytes = 0x1000. Audio start in ITCM 0x1CF9C-0x1D04E: handlers are registered through 0x10052 (-> 0x800C1568) with priority 7: DMA channel 3 -> 0x80003409, channel 4 -> 0x800034A9; NVIC enables IRQ 3 and 4; SAI receive then transmit is enabled through veneers 0x10048 (-> 0x80002D90) and 0x1003E (-> 0x80002DF8), which have the shape of the NXP SDK SAI_RxEnable/SAI_TxEnable (set RE/TE, and the partner side when synchronous); transmit sources 0x20000000 + bank x 0x1000 (+0x2000 per lane, bank index [0x80591D5C]), receive destination 0x20008000 + bank x 0x800 (bank index [0x80591D58]); SERQ (0x400E801B) is written for channels 3, 2, 1, 0, then 4. Channel 4 handler 0x800034A8 (no direct callers) calls 0x800D316C([0x80591D54], 2), clears DONE and the interrupt of channel 4 (CDNE, CINT), sets TCD4 DADDR (0x400E9090) to 0x20008000 + [0x80591D58] x 0x800 and writes SERQ for channel 4 again. Each of the two enable veneers has one direct call in the image. Neither image holds the constant 0x400E801A (CERQ) or a movw/movt pair for it, but APP1 has eDMA driver code that keeps the base 0x400E8000 in a handle (for example a create-handle routine at 0x80037B18), so a stop of channel 4 through such a handle is not ruled out. Not found: who reads the receive banks at 0x20008000 (resampling, a level meter?); no movw/movt pair outside the start code and the channel 4 handler builds that address, and readers through a pointer, for example whatever 0x800D316C wakes, are not traced. What the 16 slots carry was seen on a unit: hw.bmc.rx-slots.

facts.claim: What the second processor sends back on SAI1 receive (hw.periph.sai-dma), as seen on one unit: sound arrives all the time, not only while resampling. Slots 1 and 2 (indices 0 and 1 of the 16 int16 values of a frame) are the final output after BUS 4: pads, the EXT SOURCE input and the BUS 3/4 effects; slot 2 is the left channel and slot 1 the right (checked with panning). They are taken before the VOLUME knob: VOLUME, even at 0, did not change the numbers. Slots 3 and 4 carry the pads without the input and without the BUS 3/4 effects (where they sit relative to BUS 1/2 was not checked); slots 5-16 were all zero every time. Peaks over two receive banks (about 2.7 ms), shown 4 times a second, slots 1-4 in dBFS: silence all zero; a melodic sample with no effects -14, -17, -13, -16; a pattern with effects on BUS 3/4 -3, -2, -14, -13; only the EXT SOURCE input -13, -13, zero, zero. On a loud pattern the output peaked at -0.1 dBFS on both channels and never reached full scale (32767); that the output has a ceiling (a limiter or headroom in the second processor) is a hypothesis. Open: whether slots 1-2 are bit for bit what RESAMPLE records, what exactly slots 3-4 are, and whether this holds on other units or firmware versions. The emulator cannot show any of this: it has no second processor.

facts.claim: How the display is driven: the SSD1309 (hw.display) sits on LPSPI4 at 0x403A0000, chip select 0, with its data/command line on GPIO2 pin 1 (DR_SET 0x401BC084, DR_CLEAR 0x401BC088, mask 2: low for commands, high for data). The firmware sends a frame from a command table at 0x83FF1000: horizontal addressing (20 00), then columns 21 00 7F and pages 22 00 07, then 1024 data bytes, one per column of each 8-row page, bit 0 the top row. A mod can draw without the firmware by polling the port: DMA requests off (DER 0x1C), FIFOs emptied (CR 0x10 bits 8-9), flags cleared (SR 0x14), 8-bit frames with receive masked in TCR (0x60), each byte into TDR (0x64) when the transmit FIFO count in FSR (0x5C) is below 12, and the D/C pin moved only after FSR and SR bit 24 show the port idle. Put DER and TCR back afterwards if the firmware is to go on.

facts.claim: Effect parameters travel to the second processor as Roland DT1 packets over LPUART3: 0x800CD3A0 builds the request, encoder 0x800D8118, sender 0x800D93F0. Slot TYPE address is 02 02 00 (08+2 x slot). Parameter address is 03 (q>>7) (q&7F) offset, with q = 5 x (ID-1) + slot and offset 2 x parameter index, value as two nibbles, checksum minus sum mod 128. Reverb (ID 10) thus falls on 2D+slot, Lo-fi (ID 20) on 5F+slot.

evidence.label: EMULATOR

facts.claim: Bytes from the second processor arrive by LPUART3 interrupt (vector 0x98, stub 0x800400C8, handler 0x80090F58 with control table 0x833B708C) into a byte ring. The task loop at 0x800EBAE4 dispatches four-byte packets through the 11-entry table at 0x800EBC00 (hw.bmc.rx-table). Entry 0 is the service dispatcher 0x800665A8; its packets and address cases are described in hw.bmc.service. Other entries handle other packet channels. The nested status table under service packet 01 FF 00 value is not itemised here.

facts.claim: All LEDs share one path. 0x800D4910(idx, mode, rgb), 635 call sites, idx 0-49 of which 0-15 are pads, caches colour at 0x80BBCC34 and mode at 0x80BBCCFC and sends only on change. It calls 0x800A7DB0, which uses table 0x801E4354, then 0x8008CCC0(channel, mode, value), which makes a 4 byte message [1, cmd, channel, value] with cmd 1, 0, 6, 7, 8, 9 for modes 0-5 (a tbb at 0x8008CCD8), sent by 0x800D93F0 over LPUART3. The cache at 0x80BBCC34 and 0x80BBCCFC is written by stock code around 0x8003E1xx, 0x800C4Dxx and 0x800D49xx before anything is sent; a hook on the send 0x800A7DB0 (hk.site.led) sees the changes but leaves the cache as it is, so after a mod's own lights the cache still says what the stock last wanted.

facts.claim: USB: the board has a USB2422 2-port hub (IC6). A computer sees the hub (0424:2422) with two devices behind it: 0582:0281, a composite USB audio and MIDI device, and 0582:02E7, a CDC-ACM serial port named 'Roland SP-404MKII', which Roland's app and SparkyMK2 use for files and parameters (hw.usb.link). Third-party notes say the main chip provides the serial device and the second processor the audio and MIDI; that split is not checked here. No send path from APP1 to USB-MIDI has been found; sysex at 0x800CD3A0 goes to LPUART3. The USB stack in APP1 and its descriptors are not read.

facts.claim: The CDC serial device (hw.usb) runs at 921600 baud, 8N1, and carries framed messages in both directions: a 12-byte short message (kind 0x12, up to 7 payload bytes, their count in byte 11, which must not be 0) or a 16-byte header plus payload (kind 0x13); host 0x60, unit 0xE0; channel 5 for control and parameters, channel 6 for a POSIX-like file API (open, read, write, seek, stat, opendir and so on) with SysEx-shaped payloads. The file API serves two volumes: the unit's own storage under /SP404REMOTE// (projects, samples, factory data: the B: drive of st.storage.drives) and the SD card under / (IMPORT, EXPORT, BKUP and update files: the A: drive). A status poll answers with the project, bank, selected pad and the frames played by the sounding pad; the unit sends nothing by itself when a pad is hit, so following it means polling. The unit computes waveform peaks on request (min and max per point), which fits the stock peak service in st.chop.waveform (a guess). Edits are acknowledged even when they fail; the failure follows as a separate message with a negative code, and bank protect is enforced by Roland's app, not by the unit. For mods this is a possible way to get data out of a running unit without its card: a mod could write a file to B: and a computer could read it over this link; not tried.

facts.claim: The first 0x80000 bytes of the main processor's flash hold its loader (the version screen calls it UPD1), which no update package contains. facts.claim: Whether the loader starts APP1 or its own update screen is decided by one processor pin, read within the first instructions after reset and before the loader unpacks itself: pad GPIO_AD_B0_02 is muxed as GPIO1_IO02 (0x401F80C4 = 5), made an input, and bit 2 of 0x401B8000 is read. Bit set: the loader goes on to its update screen. Bit clear: it jumps to APP1. Nothing in APP1 takes part in this decision, so a broken APP1 cannot block the way into the update screen.

facts.claim: The loader checks nothing in APP1 before starting it: no checksum, signature, header or length. It branches to 0x60080001. So any file written as APP1 will be started, and the only integrity check a mod author has is comparing the hash of the file on the card.

facts.claim: The loader turns all three watchdogs off in its first instructions (WDOG1 0x400B8000, WDOG2 0x400D0000, RTWDOG 0x400BC000), before it decides between APP1 and the update screen. So nothing resets a unit whose APP1 hangs unless APP1 itself starts a watchdog; whether stock APP1 does is not established here. Together with fault vectors that only return (hw.faults.vectors) this is why a crash looks like a frozen unit, and why a mod that wants to survive its own faults must bring its own fault screen or reset.

facts.claim: How the unit boots, read from its registers: SRC_SBMR2 is 0x02000009, so the boot mode pins select Internal Boot (BMOD 10), and SRC_SBMR1 and the boot configuration fuses are zero, which selects serial NOR flash on FlexSPI. The debug port is not closed by fuses. The secret key words read as 0xBADABADA, which is how the chip answers for words closed to reading.

facts.claim: There may be a way back for a unit whose loader was erased, without opening it. In Internal Boot mode (hw.boot.mode) the processor's ROM jumps to its Serial Downloader, on USB or UART, when booting from flash fails, and with secure boot off it would accept an image from a computer. Nobody has tried this on an SP-404MKII: it is not known whether the processor's USB port reaches the unit's connector through the on-board hub in that state. Treat it as a hope, not a plan, and never erase a loader to find out.

facts.claim: A normal APP1 update by the loader erases exactly flash offsets 0x80000-0x3FEFFF (895 sectors of 4 KB) and then writes the file from 0x80000 in 256 byte pages until the file ends. The loader's own area below 0x80000 is not touched, and the last sector 0x3FF000 is never erased. There is no size limit in the write loop: the erased room is 0x37F000 bytes (3,665,920), so an APP1 must not be larger. A longer file would be written over the unerased sector at 0x3FF000 and then past the end of the 4 MB chip; what happens there was not tried and may brick the unit. This agrees with the owner's stalled updates in hw.update.stalled: only the application area was erased.

facts.claim: Files that can brick a unit if they are on the SD card. SP404MKII_APP1W.bin: when no SP404MKII_APP1.bin is present the loader offers it as WHOLE, erases the flash from offset 0 (its own code included) up to 0x3FEFFF and writes the file from 0; an interrupted or wrong file leaves no loader. SP404MKII_APP0W.bin: sent to the BMC in place of the normal APP0; what the BMC does with it is not known. MIRXRT1060-EVK.bin and SP404MKII_APP1U.bin are used by factory service commands that exist in APP1 (hw.service.loader-erase). None of these belongs on a user's card, and a mod or tool must never create them.

facts.claim: A program on a computer can write files to the SD card over USB, without the card leaving the unit: the file API of hw.usb.link serves the card's root, where update files live, and SparkyMK2 writes into IMPORT there. So such a program could also put one of the files of hw.update.whole-files on the card, and the next update would act on it. Writing those names over USB was not tried, and must not be: any host tool that writes to the card should refuse them as package does (docs/SAFETY.md).

facts.claim: APP1 itself carries factory service code that can erase the loader, and a mod must never call or hook it. In stock 5.52: 0x80065838 (console command fnu) erases flash 0-0x7EFFF first and only then opens a:/SP404MKII_APP1U.bin; 0x80064E48 (fnc) erases the whole chip through 0x8019D348; 0x80064E70 (fnv) and 0x8017D3C8 write a:MIRXRT1060-EVK.bin from offset 0 after a whole-chip erase. They are reached from a text console whose input was not found on USB, and nothing in normal use calls them; a stray jump into them would brick the unit. A cautious mod can put a return at their entries: `movs r0,#0; bx lr` over the first four bytes of each of the four, which is the one change the tools allow there (`"kind": "disable"`). The three low-level flash routines under them stay untouched, since stock code may use them for its own writes. The loader carries a similar console of its own.

facts.claim: Both directions of the link to the second processor carry 4-byte packets shaped like USB-MIDI events: the low nibble of the first byte says how many of the next three bytes are meant (4 = three bytes of a longer message, 5, 6, 7 = its last one, two or three bytes), so a Roland system-exclusive message is cut into such packets. The sender 0x800D93F0(buffer, length) has about 300 callers and every one passes a multiple of 4 bytes. In memory a packet is one little-endian word, so the first byte on the wire is the low byte of the word.

facts.claim: Packets from the second processor are taken as words from a ring (0x8059275C) by a task loop at 0x800EBAE4, which picks a handler by the high nibble of the first byte from a table of 11 function pointers at 0x800EBC00: entry 0 is the service dispatcher 0x800665A8, entries 1-7 and 10 are 0x80066318, entry 8 is 0x80066278, entry 9 is 0x80067920. Replacing those 11 words is enough to see every incoming packet before stock does; a mod that does so must still call the handler stock would have called. The interrupt and ring path are described in hw.bmc.rx.

facts.claim: The second processor talks to APP1 on a service channel of packets 01 FF address value, handled by 0x800665A8 through a 256-way jump table at 0x800665C6 indexed by the address byte. Seen in the table: 00 a status byte, 04 a flag, 10-16 and 20-26 groups of values, 30-43 and 50-63 the characters of two version strings, 70-84 further values, 90 an acknowledge, FE a byte converted by subtracting 0x30 and stored as a word at 0x82DFFC84 (handler 0x800668C4), FF the SHIFT key. A different packet, 01 FE 20 value, calls 0x80056C20 and stores its value as a word at 0x80249A64 (0x800667D4-0x800667EC); it is not the FF/FE table case. Most addresses do nothing. What each value means beyond these names has not been worked out.
